messages.subject: plyr installation problem
parts:
Hi - I just posted my first message on this group after becoming a
member - I recieved an email copy of my message but don't see it
appear in the topic list. Sorry for duplicating, but here's another
attempt:

I'm trying to run install.packages("plyr") and get the following
error:

Warning message:
In getDependencies(pkgs, dependencies, available, lib) :
package 'plyr' is not available

My R version 2.10.1 and I'm running this on linux. I've tried a couple
of different mirrors. Can anyone help?

thanks!

This is likely explained by the requirements listed:

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/plyr/index.html

(Note the minimum R version is 2.11 :-)

You just have to upgrade R to the latest, and try again. You'll want
to upgrade your R install anyway (not just for plyr), since (most) R
packages usually track the latest version of R, and it's almost always
best to use the latest/greatest version.

Are you allowed to compile your own software into your local/home directory?

It's pretty straightforward to compile R from source and dump it
somewhere that you have control over.

I always create a ~/sw folder that I use to install custom stuff into.
If you download the sources for R-2.12.1 you can compile/install it
quite easily.

Assuming your on a linux machine make yourself a ~/sw/src directory, then:

$ cd ~/sw/src
$ curl -O http://cran.cnr.Berkeley.edu/src/base/R-2/R-2.12.1.tar.gz
$ mkdir Rbuild
$ cd Rbuild
$ ../R-2.12.1/configure --prefix=~/sw
$ make && make install

(more or less).

Add ~/sw/bin to your PATH, and 10 mins later you're ready to rock.

-steve
